texts.preamble: Gangadhara Shenoy vs Unknown on 8 February, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 8Th Day Of February 2016/19Th Magha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 2430 of 2011 ( ) --------------------------------- Crl.A 115/2008 of Addl.Sessn.Court (Adhoc-Ii)Kasaragode Cc 238/2005 of C.J.M.,Kasaragod Revision Petitioner/Appellant/Accused: ------------------------------------------------------------- Gangadhara Shenoy, Aged 32 Years, S/O.M.Krishna Govinda Shenoy Shenoy Bazar, X-351 Uppala Mangalppady Grama Panchayath, Kasaragod Taluk. By Adv. Sri.T.G.Rajendran Respondents/Complainant & State ------------------------------------------------------- 1. Food Inspector, Kasaragod Circle, Mangalpady Grama Panchayath 2. texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 14.1.2005 at about 2.45 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 550 gram of gingelly oil from the shop of the revision petitioner. After sampling as per the rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P11 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for gingelly oil under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and therefore, the same was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P19 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 was examined and Ext.D1 was marked for the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P11 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P11 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused. The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also Gangadhara Shenoy vs Unknown on 8 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6114813/ 2 affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
